children: Preorders for Apple's foldable iPhone Duo suggest that demand is higher than expected, Yorkville Ives analysts write in a note. Shipping estimates for the phone were slipping to January across all models and colors just minutes after preorders opened on Friday. This is "a clear sign that demand at a $1,999 entry price is running well ahead of what anyone expected," they write, adding that the demand "reinforces our view that the Duo is the first major new hardware innovation out of Cupertino since the AirPods a decade ago." The volume of iPhones that have gone without upgrades for more than four years suggests that demand could stay high "well into 2027," the analysts add, projecting 20 million to 25 million units in 2027. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)
